---
title: "t-tests for two samples and for gains"
date: "2027-02-18"
---

## Goals

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

- Run a t-test for two independent samples, with a pooled variance
- Run a t-test on gains, and say why pairing helps
- Say what a gain alone can't tell you, and why control groups exist

## Reading

- {{< fa book >}} Before session 1: Chapter 10. Skip Hartley's F-max test (in 10-3) and r² (in 10-4).
- {{< fa book >}} Before session 2: Chapter 11. Skip r² (in 11-4).

::: {.callout-note}
## The book and our slides

- **The book:** writes the pooled variance as s²_p. **Our slides:** write σ̂²_p.
- **The book:** analyzes before-and-after gains in one group as evidence that a treatment worked. **Our slides:** without a control group, a gain also includes growth that would have happened anyway. Session 2 shows how much that matters for Mindspark.
:::
